knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```{r}
#| label: setup-rjd3production
library("rjd3production")
```

The {rjd3production} package is useful for setting up a production pipeline for seasonally adjusted time series.

Before creating a production pipeline, you must set up a working environment as an R project. The `init_env()` function creates the following default structure:

- a `data/` folder: raw data
- a `Workspaces/` folder: workspaces
- an `output/` folder: the output time series, tables and graphs
- a `specs/` folder: workspace-specific specifications (calendar regressors, outliers, etc.)
- a `BQ/` folder: quality reports and decision files
- a DESCRIPTION file to manage the project’s dependencies
- a `.lintr` file for static code analysis (formatting best practices)
- a README.md file to describe the process
- a Git project structure

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| label: init-project

path_project <- tempfile(pattern = "my_sa_project")
init_env(path = path_project)
```

In this vignette, we will create a production pipeline using the ABS dataset from the {rjd3toolkit} package.
The dataset is also available as the file `ABS.csv` at `{r} system.file("extdata", "ABS.csv", package = "rjd3providers")` in the {rjd3providers} package.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| label: setup-rjd3toolkit

library("rjd3toolkit")
path_ABS <- system.file("extdata", "ABS.csv", package = "rjd3providers")
my_data <- ABS[, seq_len(3L)]
colnames(my_data) <- substr(colnames(my_data), start = 2L, stop = 12L)
```

## Selection of Calendar Regressors

If the time series are sensitive to calendar effects, these effects can be corrected using calendar regressors.

To do this, refer to the `td-selection` vignette, which explains how to select the optimal set of regressors for each time series and how to generate the `td` table describing the correspondence between the time series and the selected set of calendar regressors.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: select-td

td <- select_td(my_data)
```

## Creating a workspace

We will use the {rjd3workspace} package for functions related to the creation and manipulation of workspaces.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| label: setup-rjd3workspace

library("rjd3workspace")
```

To create a new workspace, you can either create an empty one and populate it, or create it directly from a dataset.

If you use external variables, regressors, or a custom calendar, be sure to place all of these within a `modeling context.

At INSEE, we use the `create_insee_context()` function to create our `contexts`:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: create-context

my_context <- create_insee_context(s = my_data[, 1L])
```

We will use the {rjd3x13} package to create the X13 specifications.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| label: setup-rjd3x13

library("rjd3x13")
```

- Option 1: Create a workspace from scratch

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: create-ws-from-0

jws <- jws_new(modelling_context = my_context)
jsap <- jws_sap_new(jws, "Nouveau SAP")
add_sa_item(
    jsap = jsap,
    name = "Première série",
    x = my_data[, 1L],
    spec = x13_spec()
)
add_sa_item(
    jsap = jsap,
    name = "Seconde série",
    x = my_data[, 2L],
    spec = x13_spec()
)
#... avec autant de commande que de séries
```

- Option 2: Create a workspace from a dataset

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: create-ws-from-data

jws <- create_ws_from_data(my_data)
set_context(jws, create_insee_context(s = my_data))
```

If you want to use calendar regressors, you must assign the previously selected set to each series:
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: assign-td

jws_compute(jws)
assign_td(td = td, jws = jws, spec_type = c("Estimation", "Reference"))
```

Above, the regressors are specified in the reference specification (Reference Spec) and in the estimation specification (Estimation Spec). These concepts are explained [here](https://prod.jdemetra.org/p1-overview#sec-concept-specification) and [here](https://prod.jdemetra.org/p4-appendices#comp-specs).

Don’t forget to update the workspace metadata with the path to the raw data:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: update-ts-metadata

add_raw_data_path(jws, path_ABS, delimiter = "COMMA")
```

Finally, we can save our workspace!

It will stop being just a Java Virtual Object and become a set of (XML) files.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| label: save-workspace

path_ws <- file.path(path_project, "Workspaces", "workspace_travail", "my_ws.xml")
save_workspace(jws, path_ws, replace = TRUE)
```

## Using Cruncher for Estimation and Output Generation

When using a workspace structure (benefit: having data that can be read by the graphical interface), JDemetra+ [Cruncher](https://doc.jdemetra.org/t-production-tools-cruncher-qr) allows you to automate two important operations:

1. Updating the raw data from the data file

2. Updating the seasonally adjusted data by taking into account new raw data points and/or revisions to the recent past. You can choose a refresh policy to update the seasonal adjustment model with varying degrees of constraint. For more details, see the [documentation](https://doc.jdemetra.org/a-rev-policies).
